jobs.title: Credit Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

SoFi’s Credit team manages credit risk activities for our lending products (Student Loan Refinance, Private Student Loan, Personal Loan, Credit Card, and Mortgage) - including credit strategies/policies for new account origination and portfolio management, collections/recovery strategies and operations, and risk and operational data science and analytics. The team designs data-driven strategies to ensure the growth in lending is consistent with the company’s risk appetite and helps create the products and experiences that put our members’ interests first.

The Credit Strategy Lead will work in the Credit team and have responsibilities to analyze and evaluate data to develop and propose value-added credit risk strategies and models for SoFi’s lending products, including Personal Loan, Student Loan Refinance, Private Student Loan, and Credit Card.

The Credit Strategy Lead will collaborate with cross-functional teams such as Business Units, Capital Markets, Product and Engineering, and use business knowledge and quantitative and analytical skills to drive revenue, control risk, and provide value to the company and consumers.

The ideal candidate will possess a data-driven analytics background and the strategic acumen to direct a function that draws strategic insights from data using database and statistical analysis tools to inform decisions and support SoFi’s overarching strategic goals relative to loss prevention and profit optimization. They bring new ways of thinking, data sources, technologies, and capabilities to SoFi.

What you’ll do:

- Innovate… Bring your brightest ideas to building risk strategies. This means you will architect the pre-screen and underwriting strategies.

- Data Driven… Your deep analysis will power the future of lending with an optimal real-time data ecosystem – including multi-product internal, bureau, third-party, and alternative data sources and uses.

- Iterate, learn, innovate… We are all responsible for innovation and must embrace data-driven decisions.

- Control the Risk and Drive Performance Outcomes … Understand credit risk and develop approaches to mitigate loss and responsibly grow revenue. Monitor the performance of strategies and portfolios. Document and communicate results and escalate issues as necessary. Identify gaps/opportunities and drive actions.

- Grow, Grow, Grow!… Be inspired by dynamic leaders and our rapidly growing business. We want YOU to be an inspired leader of tomorrow, so we are recruiting the best, brightest, and passionately quantitative team members.

What you’ll need:

- 4+ years of related experience

- Business acumen and work experience in the consumer lending business (loans or credit cards)

- Direct experience in the credit strategy analytical life cycle, including strategy and decision tree development, presentation, implementation validation, and post-implementation monitoring

- Proven analytical skills in conducting sophisticated analysis using customer performance data, bureau attributes, and other 3rd party variables to solve business problems

- Proficient skills in Excel, SQL and Python

- A demonstrated ability to synthesize and communicate analysis to business partners and senior management

- High motivation to drive results, eager to learn, and able to work collaboratively in a fluid environment

- Knowledge/skills in analytical and modeling techniques such as Decision Trees, regression, logistic regression, A/B Testing, and Tableau

- Preferred: 4+ years of consumer lending credit strategy work experience

- Preferred: Experience in analyzing and testing credit strategies or models to meet the fair lending requirements

- Preferred: Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) with a quantitative major such as Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or Computer Science

jobs.title: Direct Mail Marketing Manager (Contract)
jobs.description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The role:

SoFi is seeking an energetic, organized, and resourceful Direct Mail Marketing Manager for a one-year contract to manage the end-to-end direct mail creative process for the SoFi Credit Card product, from strategy and planning through creative development, stakeholder review, approval, production, and tracking. This role will also analyze campaign performance and provide recommendations to optimize future direct mail strategies and creative.

At SoFi, you’ll become part of a new kind of finance company whose ambition is to help our members achieve financial independence and reach their goals. We aim to be at the center of our members’ financial lives and help every member get their money right. We created student loan refinancing, addressing the biggest financial challenge of a new generation through a modern approach to lending and personal finance. Next, we expanded our products and services across loans, investing, and cash management. SoFi has achieved significant growth, with ambitious plans ahead, but to continue this growth, we need great talent. And that starts with you.

What you’ll do:

This role owns four core areas of responsibility:

1. Creative Strategy & Planning

-
Lead end-to-end creative strategy and execution for Credit Card direct mail campaigns, partnering with Product Marketing Manager (PMM) to align initiatives with business goals, priorities, and growth objectives.

-
Lead quarterly creative planning with the creative agency, using audience insights, customer behavior, performance data, and test-and-learn principles to develop strategic recommendations for the Product Marketing Manager.

-
Lead upfront data and audience planning with DM Data Strategy, Marketing Data Science and agency team defining targeting, segmentation, personalization, measurement requirements, and data inputs that inform the creative strategy, testing plan, and campaign brief.

-
Own the creative roadmap and partner with the creative agency to develop compelling messaging, visual storytelling, offers, personalization, branding, and calls to action.

2. Campaign & Production Management

-
Serve as the day-to-day campaign lead and primary liaison among Product Marketing Manager, the creative and data strategy agency, DM Data Strategy, Marketing Data Science, other internal stakeholders, and print vendors.

-
Serve as the lead DM representative in Credit Card business unit meetings, Marketing Data Science handoff meetings, and other recurring meetings. Prepare slides as needed, capture key decisions and action items, and distribute notes to appropriate stakeholders.

-
Translate approved strategies into actionable campaign plans, creative briefs, testing plans, and production requirements.

-
Manage monthly direct mail tests and creative variations, ensuring audience definitions, segmentation, data requirements, personalization, and creative variants are aligned and executable.

-
Own campaign timelines and the shared production calendar, including data due dates, creative milestones, review rounds, release dates, print dates, and drop dates.

-
Manage assets, versioning, production samples, dependencies, risks, and bottlenecks to ensure campaigns launch accurately and on time.

-
Maintain the monthly campaign matrix, including audience targeting, creative variations, testing plans, data requirements, and other campaign details.

-
Partner with Marketing Data Science to update campaign matrices and verify that targeting and personalization information is accurate before each drop.

-
Lead weekly status meetings with Product Marketing Managers, including agenda development, stakeholder alignment, and action-item follow-up.

3. Compliance, Quality & Operations

-
Lead the Compliance and Legal review process for direct mail materials, partnering with Product Marketing and the creative agency to ensure executions meet regulatory, disclosure, brand, and business requirements.

-
Manage creative review and quality control across messaging, data, personalization, offers, URLs, disclosures, and final production files.

-
Serve as the central point of accountability for ensuring every campaign is accurate, compliant, data-aligned, approved, and production-ready.

-
Manage campaign production and postage costs, partnering with the DM billing team to keep campaigns within budget.

4. Performance, Insights & Competitive Intelligence

-
Partner with Marketing Data Science, analytics, and the creative agency to evaluate campaign and creative test results against product and business goals.

-
Translate audience, performance, and campaign data into actionable insights that inform creative recommendations, messaging, offers, personalization, segmentation, and future test strategies.

-
Lead weekly Product Marketing Manager performance updates and monthly reporting, presenting results and optimization recommendations to Product Marketing and cross-functional stakeholders.

-
Apply campaign learnings to improve future direct mail initiatives and inform the creative roadmap.

-
Build and maintain a competitive direct mail library, monitoring competitor activity, creative trends, offers, formats, personalization, and audience strategies.

-
Share monthly competitive and performance insights with the broader Marketing organization to inform future campaign and product marketing strategy.

What you’ll need:

-
Bachelor's degree with 4+ years of project management experience, preferably supporting direct mail or other marketing campaigns within financial services or another highly regulated industry.

-
Experience partnering with cross-functional teams to execute complex, multi-channel campaigns and operational initiatives.

-
Experience managing high-volume direct mail, CRM, lifecycle, or integrated marketing creative execution, ideally within financial services, credit cards, banking, or another highly regulated industry.

-
Strong project and production management skills with the ability to manage multiple campaigns, creative versions, stakeholders, and deadlines simultaneously.

-
Highly proficient in Google Workspace, particularly Google Sheets, Docs, Slides, Gmail, and Calendar, Tableau, Snowflake; comfortable building and maintaining detailed trackers and production workflows.

-
Strong understanding of creative development, production, version control, review/approval processes, and vendor management.

-
Experience working directly with Legal, Compliance, Creative, Marketing, Analytics, Data, and external production vendors.

-
Strong attention to detail and a high level of ownership, particularly when managing personalized credit card communications where small errors can have significant downstream impact.

-
Comfortable working in a test-and-learn environment, using campaign performance data to inform future creative decisions.

-
Excellent communication and organizational skills with the ability to keep senior stakeholders informed while driving day-to-day execution.

-
Financial services or credit card marketing experience strongly preferred, particularly familiarity with regulated marketing, compliance reviews, disclosures, and credit-related communications.

jobs.title: Independent Risk Management Director, Investment Products
jobs.description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The role:

SoFi is seeking an energetic, detail-oriented, self-motivated, and intellectually curious Independent Risk Management (IRM) Director to support the growth of our Invest business.  Your success in this role will rely on deep subject matter expertise in broker-dealer, investment advisory matters, and retail investment product risks. This person will serve as the senior second-line risk leader responsible for independent risk oversight of the Invest business. This role will act as the primary risk partner to Invest leadership, providing credible challenge, strategic risk advisory, and oversight across all material risk categories associated with the business, excluding Compliance Risk, which is overseen by a dedicated Invest Compliance organization. Specifically, the Director will operate in close partnership with Compliance leadership in a coordinated coverage model to ensure comprehensive and effective risk oversight.

Will look for this leader to leverage their comprehensive understanding of risk management and the mitigating controls needed across risk types - including operational, fraud, technology, credit and third-party.  You will apply lessons learned from peers across the industry - both benchmarking against industry leaders as well as learning from those who have under-performed, ensuring strong risk governance, diversified exposures, and rigorous controls.

As part of the Second Line of Defense (2LOD), this individual will provide oversight across risk types for all product and feature launches as well as partner with 1LOD risk owners on ensuring we are appropriately identifying, monitoring, and mitigating risks as part of our framework programs as we scale and grow this business.  The ideal candidate is comfortable challenging business assumptions, escalation decisions, and risk-taking activities to ensure alignment with approved risk appetite.

By joining SoFi, you'll become part of a forward-thinking company that is transforming financial services for the better. We offer the excitement of a rapidly growing startup with the stability of an industry leading leadership team.

What you’ll do:

- Serve as the accountable 2LOD Risk Manager for the Invest business, maintaining an enterprise-wide view of Invest’s risk profile including key risk themes and control effectiveness.

- Become a trusted advisor to senior business leaders on risk implications of strategic decisions, product expansion, operational changes, and emerging risks.

- Represent Independent Risk Management in executive forums related to Invest strategy, governance, and risk management.

- Present risk assessments and recommendations to senior management committees, executive leadership, and Board-level governance forums, as appropriate.

- Provide hands-on independent oversight and credible challenge across consumer and retail investment products: self-directed brokerage, robo-advisory, options trading, IPOs, alternative investments, Composer trading algorithms, margin lending, and broker-dealer clearing/introducing broker relationships.

- Oversee aggregate portfolio risk trends, including:

- Operational (trade processing/settlement/service failures, reconciliation breaks, corporate action errors),

- Fraud (targeted risk assessments across all attack vectors),

- Third party (vendor diligence, outages and cyber incidents, service degradation, concentration risk),

- Technology & platform (trading outages, mobile app/API failures, data quality issues),

- Product (new product introduction, portfolio construction errors, rebalancing failures, product design flaws, unexpected concentration exposures),

- Credit (margin lending), and

- Model

- Identify thematic and emerging risk trends and ensure timely root-cause analysis, corrective action plans, and sustainable remediation.

- Collaborate with business units, Enterprise Risk Management, Compliance, AML and other functional teams to optimize the Enterprise Risk Appetite and tolerance.  This includes understanding root causes for Key Risk Indicator (KRIs) breaches against tolerance thresholds.

- Support post-launch reviews and continuous control enhancements as the business scales.

- Benchmark risk practices against peer institutions and incorporate lessons learned from industry events or control failures.

What you’ll need:

- 10+ years of experience in Risk Management, Operational Risk, Enterprise Risk, Product Risk, Audit, Compliance, or related control functions.

- Broker-Dealer experience and Consumer Investment Product experience

- Demonstrated experience supporting brokerage, investment advisory, wealth management, digital investing, and/or securities businesses.

- Demonstrated experience providing independent oversight and credible challenge to senior business leaders.

- Experience leading cross-functional risk assessments and governance processes for complex financial services businesses.

- Experience interacting directly with regulators, executive management, and Board committees.

- Exceptional interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills

- Strong leadership, collaboration, influencing and organizational skills with attention to detail

What success looks like:

- Establishing a comprehensive and forward-looking view of Invest business risks.

- Influencing business strategy and product development through effective risk advisory and challenge.

- Ensuring risks remain within Board-approved appetite while enabling business growth.

- Driving timely identification, escalation, and remediation of material issues.

- Maintaining strong partnerships across Invest, Compliance, Technology, Operations, Fraud, and Enterprise Risk functions.

- Demonstrating effective regulatory engagement and governance leadership.

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

The role:

As a Staff Compensation Analyst, you will play a key role in shaping SoFi Technologies’ global compensation strategy and programs to attract, retain, and motivate top talent globally. This role will lead our global job architecture, compensation structures, market benchmarking, and broad-based compensation modeling. You will use expert knowledge, market data, trends, technology, and financial analysis to develop compensation frameworks that are competitive, scalable, and aligned with our compensation philosophy.

You will be responsible for developing our annual cash and equity guidelines, modeling program budgets, and partnering with Finance on monthly stock-based compensation forecasting and analysis. You will also support the executive compensation function, working closely with the Executive Compensation Lead on Compensation Committee materials, executive compensation programs, and related disclosures.

What you’ll do:

Broad-Based Strategy & Execution

- Lead global compensation benchmarking, market pricing, and the development of compensation structures, including base salary ranges, target bonuses, and long-term incentive guidelines.

- Own and enhance SoFi’s global job architecture, including job families, career levels, job profiles, and related compensation frameworks.

- Lead job architecture maintenance and redesign projects to support organizational design, workforce planning, career development, and talent acquisition.

- Develop recommendations for annual cash and equity program budgets based on market data, business priorities, affordability, and compensation strategy.

- Develop and maintain equity guidelines and model the share usage, dilution, and stock-based compensation impact of new hire, promotion, refresh, and other equity programs.

- Partner with Finance on monthly stock-based compensation forecasting, variance analysis, and long-term planning.

- Apply country-specific market practices and regulatory considerations to ensure compensation structures are locally competitive while remaining consistent with SoFi’s global compensation philosophy.

- Monitor compensation trends, market practices, and emerging developments, providing recommendations and insights to the Compensation team and business leaders.

- Partner with People, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Talent Acquisition to ensure compensation programs support business needs and are administered consistently.

Executive Compensation Support

- Support the preparation of quarterly Compensation Committee and Board materials, including executive compensation analyses, scenario modeling, and executive-ready insights.

- Assist with the preparation of proxy disclosures, including the Compensation Discussion and Analysis and SEC-required compensation tables, in partnership with Legal, Accounting, Finance, and Investor Relations.

- Support executive compensation operations, including incentive program tracking, Compensation Committee approval materials, stock ownership policy compliance, and executive offer letter development.

- Conduct executive compensation benchmarking and market analysis using relevant survey and peer company data.

What You'll Need:

- Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, human resources, business, or a related field. An advanced degree or relevant professional certification is a plus.

- At least six years of broad-based compensation experience, including at least three years of direct experience developing job architecture, compensation structures, and market benchmarking frameworks. Executive compensation experience is preferred but not required.

- Experience owning or significantly contributing to global job architecture programs, including job families, career levels, salary structures, and incentive guidelines.

- Experience developing compensation programs for a multinational organization, including familiarity with country-specific compensation practices and structures.

- Direct experience supporting compensation programs in Latin America, including markets such as Argentina, Brazil, Ecuador, and Uruguay.

- Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, including experience building complex compensation, equity, and financial models.

- Experience modeling stock-based compensation expense, equity usage, dilution, or related financial impacts in partnership with Finance or Accounting.

- Experience using major compensation surveys and data providers, such as Radford, Willis Towers Watson, Mercer, or McLagan.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and translate findings into practical recommendations.

- Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex compensation concepts clearly to different audiences.

- Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive and confidential information with discretion.

- Strong cross-functional partnership skills and experience working with stakeholders across People, Finance, Legal, Accounting, Compliance, and Talent Acquisition.
